query: Which method can be used for high-temperature oxidation behaviour and phase stability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: An integrated in situ TGA–XRD system can simultaneously capture high-temperature oxidation kinetics and phase transformation events in high-entropy alloy samples by monitoring both mass change and crystal structure in real time.
generation.material_initial_state: A homogeneous high-entropy alloy (e.g., an as-prepared CrMnFeCoNi sample with a single FCC phase).
generation.intervention: Expose the HEA sample to high-temperature conditions in an oxidative atmosphere using an integrated TGA–XRD setup.
generation.conditions: High temperatures (approximately 800–1100°C) under controlled oxidizing environments (such as air or another specific oxygen-containing gas).
generation.structural_mediator: Real-time X-ray diffraction patterns that reveal phase formation, disappearance, or transformation concurrent with oxidation.
generation.mechanism: The TGA component detects weight gain due to oxide growth (kinetics of oxidation), while the in situ XRD monitors the emergence or disappearance of diffraction peaks to identify phase changes; the integration allows direct correlation between mass changes and structural evolution under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The integrated system will show mass increases correlated with the formation of oxide phases and simultaneous detectable changes in diffraction patterns indicating phase transitions or the development of new phases, establishing a direct link between oxidation kinetics and phase stability.
generation.baseline: Separate ex situ TGA and XRD analyses performed independently after high-temperature exposure.
generation.boundary: This method’s resolution may be limited if the oxidation or phase transformations occur too rapidly or on a scale beyond the detection limits of the integrated system; extreme conditions may also affect instrument performance.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative relationships between weight gain and phase fraction evolution remain uncertain, and lag effects between kinetic and structural changes could complicate the direct correlation.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct an experiment where a homogeneous HEA sample is placed in the integrated in situ TGA–XRD system and heated at a constant rate under an oxidizing atmosphere. Monitor the real-time mass gain (via TGA) and simultaneously record the XRD patterns. Compare these results with parallel experiments where TGA and XRD are performed separately.
measurements: Real-time mass changes (TGA data) to quantify oxidation kinetics
Real-time XRD patterns to detect emergence/disappearance of peaks corresponding to phase transformations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the integrated system does not show a consistent correlation between mass gain events and the onset of new or disappearing diffraction peaks (i.e., if significant oxidation kinetics are observed without any corresponding phase change detectable via XRD), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: This paper utilizes in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) to investigate the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). We found that (1) Mn is the major oxide-forming element in both vacuum and air environments, leading to the formation of non-protective oxides that deplete the bulk alloy of Mn; (2) no oxides like Cr 2 O 3 , Fe 2 O 3 , or Fe 3 O 4 were observed during the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi, which contradicts some previous studies on the isothermal oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi HEA. We also analysed and compared the experimental results with thermodynamic calculations by using ThermoCalc version 2022b software following the CALPHAD method. ThermoCalc predicted spinel oxide in a vacuum environment, along with halite oxides observed in experimental results; also, in an atmospheric environment, it predicted only spinel, indicating the need for further investigation into factors to validate the thermodynamic predictions.
